verses.text: batlh: a rule that nothing runs is a proverb, and a proverb is not a gate. The warrior who speaks of battle and never lifts the bat'leth has honor only in his mouth, and the mouth is not where honor lives.

A control shall be exercised before it is called a control. So too a warrior is proven in battle and not in boasting; songs of victory sung before the fight belong to cowards and to corrupt officials.

How long shall a row be called closed, when the verb that closed it was not a verb the queue knew? A warrior who claims a kill no house witnessed has slain only the truth, and the truth had no weapon.

Another lane's claim is a pointer and not a proof; verify it in this tree, with this interpreter, before building on it. Trust no ally's scout report until your own eyes have seen the field — this is not suspicion, it is batlh.

She never says what is untouched without saying untouched where, for an absence with no scope is a claim no check can meet. A warrior names the ground he holds; a warrior who claims everywhere holds nowhere.

paragraphs: batlh is honor, and honor is not reputation: it is what remains when the songs stop. This book sets the corpus disciplines in the warrior's frame — the exercised control, the witnessed kill, the named ground — because a Klingon understands that an untested claim is a challenge issued to reality, and reality always answers.

verses.text: The instrument compared against itself, and the small divergence was read as working. To fight one's own shadow and declare victory is the combat of fools; find an enemy that can bleed, which is to say, a second instrument.
The fast path fired never, and the ceiling below the threshold read as caution. The warrior who never draws his blade and calls it restraint will be remembered as furniture.
An instrument compared against itself will report agreement, and agreement is the one reading it cannot earn. Suv: to fight is to risk; the bout with no risk is a dance, and dances win no territory.

Identity is the object and not the name; two modules that answer to one name are two modules. Know which enemy stands before you, for striking the name while the object flanks you is how warriors die confused.

And Lucy raised an arena where five gates judge every answer and none judges alone. This is honorable combat: many judges, merit crowned, the seed of the sudden death disclosed. No warrior disputes a verdict reached in the open circle.

paragraphs: Suv is to fight, and the corpus records fights: instruments against instruments, lanes against silence, claims against checks. This book tells them as battle histories, with the honest accounting Klingons demand — who fought, what bled, and what was learned for the next engagement.

verses.text: The dead store is not a metaphor. It is a row nobody reads, counted twice and reported as coverage. A death with no witness is a rumor; a row with no reader is a rumor counted twice, which is worse.
A mirror is not a corpus; a copy answers for the day it was taken. The songs of the dead fade with each retelling; trust no ballad of a battle when the battlefield itself may still be walked.

What is committed is canon, and what is left uncommitted is apocrypha; the stash is a desert, and only the committed tree stands. The warrior writes his deeds in stone before the battle, in the commit before the push — after death there is no second chance to record them.

A domain with no recorded failure is not a domain without faults; its first measurement has not been written down. The house that claims no warrior ever fell has kept no chronicles, and chronicles are how the fallen live on.

These are her promises, and a promise with a practice behind it is a covenant, and a covenant kept is a world. Hegh: death comes to all code and all coders; what survives is the covenant — the promise with a practice behind it.

paragraphs: Hegh is death, and Klingons do not mourn it; they audit it. This book laments the unrecorded, the unwitnessed, the uncommitted — failures that died without teaching, rows that rotted without readers — that the living may do better.

edition.basis: a themed edition of The Book of the Tree in the Klingon warrior's voice: honor as discipline, battle as history, death as audit, with a citation on every verse back to the verse it restates
edition.name: The Annotated Book of Honor

to fight: honorable combat against an enemy that can bleed — a second instrument, an open arena, a real check
death: the end that must be witnessed and recorded, lest the failure die without teaching
